mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has improved monotonically from -9.7% to -3.3% over four weeks, signaling sustained recovery momentum. This trend will continue, driving RETAIL_REC further positive over the next four weeks as baseline confidence in retail activity strengthens.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 6.4 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the last 28 days, or reverses by more than 2 percentage points in any single week.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has risen consistently from 7.3% to 10.4%, indicating sustained essential-goods shopping. This behavioral shift reflects household provisioning for the holiday season, which will suppress discretionary RETAIL_REC spending as budgets are redirected to groceries.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM exceeds 9.5% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose 3.1 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining above 9.5%, or GROCERY_PHARM falls below 8.0% within the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has improved from -44.1% to -37.7% over four weeks, indicating commuting recovery. When combined with rising WORKPLACES mobility (from -16.3% to -11.4%), this dual signal predicts that foot traffic to retail zones will accelerate as workers return to offices near shopping districts.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve by >3 percentage points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 6.4 points, WORKPLACES improved 4.9 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase when both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improve simultaneously, or either series reverses by >2 points in weeks 1-2 of the forecast period.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has recovered from -20.9% to -7.3% over four weeks, approaching baseline. This seasonal pattern reflects December holiday outdoor activity in Sydney. Concurrent retail recovery suggests holiday shopping and leisure spending will sustain RETAIL_REC gains through the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS exceeds -10% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved 13.6 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase when PARKS remains above -10%, or PARKS falls below -15% in any week of the forecast period.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined from 6.3% to 4.0% over four weeks, indicating reduced home confinement. This deconfinement signal, combined with TRANSIT recovery, suggests policy restrictions are easing. Retail will benefit as mobility constraints lift, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 5.0% while TRANSIT improves by >2 points
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined 2.3 points while TRANSIT improved 6.4 points
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL does not continue declining or TRANSIT reverses by >3 points, or RETAIL_REC fails to increase in weeks 1-2 of the forecast.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility remains depressed at -11.4%, indicating incomplete office return. This persistent workplace deficit will constrain RETAIL_REC growth because weekday foot traffic near employment centers remains suppressed, limiting retail recovery momentum.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -10% for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES at -11.4% in most recent week
failure_condition: WORKPLACES exceeds -8% in any of the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 3 percentage points despite WORKPLACES remaining below -10%.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS mobility both show strong recovery, indicating outdoor and essential-goods activity. This dual shift reflects holiday-season behavioral reallocation away from discretionary retail toward parks and provisioning, suppressing RETAIL_REC despite overall mobility gains.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM exceeds 9.0% AND PARKS exceeds -10% simultaneously
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases when both GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS are elevated, or either series falls below its trigger threshold in weeks 1-2.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility at -37.7% remains severely depressed relative to other categories. This persistent transit deficit signals that public-transport-dependent retail zones remain inaccessible, creating a structural ceiling on RETAIL_REC recovery regardless of other mobility gains.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -35% in the first week of the forecast period
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -37.7%, the most depressed category
failure_condition: TRANSIT improves to above -30% within one week, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 2 percentage points in week 1 despite TRANSIT remaining below -35%.
